_readme: Every number the college model agrees on lives here, once.
Before this file existed the tuning constants sat in build_ratings.py and were
copied by hand into cfb_backtest.py, the price and sanity thresholds were copied
into cfb_card.py, and the backtest's win-loss records were pasted into
cfb_picks.py. Four copies of the same numbers, kept in step by remembering to.
'ratings', 'simulation' and 'thresholds' are hand-edited: change a value here and
every script picks it up on the next run. 'backtest' is written by cfb_backtest.py
when the manual cfb-backtest workflow runs, so re-running it updates the grades and
the card with nothing to paste.
scripts/model_state.py reads this file and falls back to the same values compiled
in, so a broken or missing file cannot stop a card being built. When that happens
the card says so in Needs attention rather than quietly using stale numbers.

_notes.half_life: games; college seasons are short so decay must be quicker
_notes.carry: prior-season carryover, eroded by the transfer portal
_notes.margin_cap: blowout cap, high enough that FBS-over-FCS games still inform the division gap
_notes.ridge_alpha: light. With a talent prior to shrink toward, heavy shrinkage only costs accuracy
_notes.min_games: below this a team cannot be estimated; bucket it
_notes.talent_pts: points per standard deviation of recruiting talent, fitted on real games
_notes.talent_cap: clip the talent z-score; no prior should be worth 25 points on its own

_notes.line_sd: our uncertainty about the true spread. The NFL card uses 3.0
_notes.margin_sd: margin around the true line at a total of 52. The NFL card uses 13.2
_notes.total_sd: points around the true total. The NFL card uses 10.4
_notes.total_tilt: |residual| = a * total + b, fitted on 762 FBS games, normalised at c
_notes.win_points: the NFL scoring scale, carried over unchanged and verified against their worked example

_notes.break_even: percent needed to profit at standard -110 pricing
_notes.game_sd: margin scatter used to turn a spread into a win probability
_notes.price_flag: a book's moneyline and spread disagreeing by this much is worth showing
_notes.price_pick: and by this much becomes a pick
_notes.price_max: the conversion is meaningless past this spread; scatter grows from 1 point to 5.5
_notes.ml_sane: a real two-sided market never gets past about this, so anything beyond is a placeholder
_notes.spplus_flag: our number against SP+ diverging by this much flags a game low information

backtest.window: 2022-2025, walk-forward, FBS vs FBS, real closing lines

record_notes.price_gap: a book's moneyline against its own spread, 3+ points
record_notes.model_gap_late: our number vs the close, weeks 5 on
record_notes.model_gap_early: our number vs the close, weeks 1-4
